RULES:
- Everything `IF NOT EXISTS`. Dev and prod already have all of it, so this must be a pure no-op against them.
- Match the existing house style of `migrations/0015_startup_schema_cleanup.sql`: a short comment block explaining why, then `BEGIN;` … `COMMIT;`.
- Column types, nullability, defaults and FK targets must match `shared/schema.ts` exactly. Include the indexes that the `pgTable` third-argument declares.
- `windcave_api_key` / `windcave_merchant_id` are credential columns — create them, never seed them.
- Do NOT run `drizzle-kit push` under any circumstances (FK columns on this branch carry rogue auto-increment defaults).
- Do NOT run `npm run db:migrate`, and do NOT apply anything to the dev database (`DATABASE_URL`) or prod (`NEON_DATABASE_URL`). I will apply it myself after review.

VERIFICATION GATE — you must actually run this, not reason about it:
Build a scratch database and apply `migrations/*.sql` to it in order, then diff the result against `shared/schema.ts`. Drift must be 0 tables and 0 columns. Use a uniquely-named scratch database on the same server as `DATABASE_URL` (e.g. `taptpay_scratch_<random>`), and DROP IT when you are done — verify the drop succeeded. Never point the check at the real dev or prod database.
Note the trap: each `migrations/*.sql` carries its own `BEGIN;`/`COMMIT;`, so if you wrap them in an outer transaction their `COMMIT` ends yours. Apply each file on its own.
A useful starting point for the drift computation exists at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-runner-workspace/c91138e1-3508-4c6d-8e3b-6b0c7689d01a/scratchpad/drift.mjs — it compares migrations to schema.ts statically. Your gate should be stronger: compare the *actual built database* against schema.ts via information_schema.

Also run `npx tsc --noEmit` (must be silent) before you finish.

Do NOT commit anything. Do NOT run `git add`. Leave the new file in the working tree.

REPORT BACK: the exact path of the file you created, the drift numbers before and after, the scratch DB name and confirmation it was dropped, and anything in `shared/schema.ts` that you could not faithfully translate into SQL.

# Plan — finish the 2026-08-09 review-and-fix pass

**Branch:** `feat/tablet-desktop-app`  **HEAD when written:** `8af83fc`
**Written:** 2026-08-10, after recovering an interrupted review that left ~1 hour of
unreviewed, uncommitted work in the tree.

This plan does two things: it **inventories what the interrupted pass actually
landed** (§2), and it **plans the whole remaining path to done** (§4). Read §1
before running anything — the tree is currently in a broken state that looks fine.

---

## 0. Provenance — why this plan exists

A review-and-fix pass ran in Codex (`gpt-5.6-sol`, reasoning effort `max`) on
**2026-08-09 between 08:33:59 and 09:36:49 UTC**. It crashed three times. The
environment reset that accompanied the crashes recreated `~/.codex` from scratch
(fresh `installation_id` and OAuth login at 03:39 on 2026-08-10), so **its session
transcripts are unrecoverable**. The 2026-08-10 resume attempt died 1.1 seconds in
on an OpenAI usage limit that does not reset until **2026-08-16 08:01**.

It committed nothing, stashed nothing, and wrote no handoff. Everything it did is
uncommitted working-tree state, and §2 of this document is the only record of it.

Attribution is established by mtime against session boundaries:

| Window | Author | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-08 11:09–11:38 | Claude (paused WIP) | 12 landing-phone scene/primitive files — the "phone realism" work paused on 2026-08-08 |
| 2026-08-09 → 07:58 | Claude, session `aca5eae5` | Committed `5022431`…`8af83fc`, then closed confirming "working tree clean apart from landing-phone WIP" |
| **2026-08-09 08:33:59 → 09:36:49** | **the interrupted review** | **everything else uncommitted — §2** |

The review was working from three written sources, none of which covers all of it:

1. `docs/PLAN-2026-08-07-subscription-pricing.md` — §5 dunning, §9 copy sweep, §11
   verification, §12 step 13 (`client/public/app` regen). Committed and authoritative.
2. The **P0–P3 plan** from the tail of session `aca5eae5`, which was never written to
   a file. Reproduced in §3 below so it stops being lost.
3. The eight "Still open" items in the `dev-db-unapplied-migrations` memory.

Everything in §2a, §2b and part of §2c was the review's **own** findings and is
covered by no prior document at all.

---

## 1. Where things actually stand (measured 2026-08-10)

```
npx tsc --noEmit                     silent
npx jest --selectProjects server     23 suites / 325 tests — all pass
npx jest --selectProjects client     33 suites / 338 tests — all pass
npm run db:migrate:status            15 applied, 3 pending, 0 drifted, 0 orphaned
node scripts/verify-landing-phone.mjs  FAILS — see §4 Step 3

### The tree is in the 2026-08-09 outage state

`shared/schema.ts` now declares `transactions.completedAt`, and the migration that
creates the column has never been applied. Drizzle's `select()` enumerates every
declared column, so:

```
db.select().from(transactions).limit(1)
  → error: column "completed_at" does not exist
```

This is the **exact failure class** that caused the 2026-08-09 "app loads forever"
incident — see the `dev-db-unapplied-migrations` memory. Two things currently mask it:

- the dev server on `:5000` (pid 184, booted 03:39 today) is serving, and printed the
  pending-migration banner exactly as the new gate is designed to. Nothing has hit a
  `transactions` query since boot, so no error has surfaced yet;
- the router-level async guard from `dc16ab9` means it now returns a fast 500 instead
  of hanging. It degrades better than last time. It is still broken.

**Nothing else in §4 may be attempted before Step 0.**

### Production

Prod is still running previously deployed code and is unaffected *today*. But
`server/index.ts` now hard-exits when migrations are pending, so **a deploy of this
tree onto an unmigrated prod database will refuse to boot**. Deploy order is fixed
by Step 9 and is not optional.

## 2. Inventory — what the interrupted pass landed (all uncommitted)

Verdicts: **KEEP** = verified, commit as-is. **RATIFY** = defensible but it decides
something that was Oliver's to decide (§3). **FINISH** = started, not complete.

caused 2026-08-09. Note it makes Step 9's ordering mandatory forever.

taking money. **Needs an explicit number from you**, even if it is 8.

a 14s deadline, asserted by test.

-- Catch-up so that `migrations/` alone can rebuild a database matching
-- shared/schema.ts. Six tables and fifteen columns are declared by Drizzle but
-- were never created by a numbered migration — they reached dev and prod by
-- hand or by an old `drizzle-kit push`, so provisioning a new environment from
-- the checked-in history produced a database the app could not run against
-- (Drizzle's `select()` enumerates every declared column).
--
-- Every statement is IF NOT EXISTS: this migration is a no-op against dev and
-- prod, which already have all of it. It records history, it does not change
-- either database. Nothing here backfills or infers data.
--
-- windcave_api_key / windcave_merchant_id are credential columns. They are
-- created empty and are never seeded.

BEGIN;

ALTER TABLE merchants
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS google_id text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS director text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS nzbn text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS custom_logo_url text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS windcave_api_key text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS windcave_merchant_id text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS theme_id text DEFAULT 'classic',
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS daily_goal numeric(10, 2) DEFAULT '500.00',
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS reset_token text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS reset_token_expiry timestamp;

-- One-off non-rent charges: `kind` distinguishes them from rent, `charge_type`
-- and `description` label them, and the two document_* columns carry the
-- optional attachment shown to the tenant at checkout.
ALTER TABLE invoices_rent_requests
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS kind text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'rent',
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS charge_type text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS description text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS document_url text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS document_name text;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS refunds (
  id serial PRIMARY KEY,
  transaction_id integer,
  merchant_id integer,
  refund_amount numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL,
  refund_reason text,
  refund_method text DEFAULT 'original_payment_method',
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
  windcave_refund_id text,
  windcave_fee_refunded numeric(10, 2) DEFAULT '0.00',
  platform_fee_refunded numeric(10, 2) DEFAULT '0.00',
  initiated_by text,
  customer_notified boolean DEFAULT false,
  completed_at timestamp,
  created_at timestamp DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT refunds_transaction_id_transactions_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (transaction_id) REFERENCES transactions(id),
  CONSTRAINT refunds_merchant_id_merchants_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (merchant_id) REFERENCES merchants(id)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS refunds_transaction_id_idx
  ON refunds (transaction_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS refunds_merchant_id_idx
  ON refunds (merchant_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS merchant_settlements (
  id serial PRIMARY KEY,
  merchant_id integer,
  settlement_period text NOT NULL,
  total_transaction_amount numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL,
  total_windcave_fees numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL,
  total_platform_fees numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL,
  net_settlement_amount numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
  settlement_date timestamp,
  created_at timestamp DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT merchant_settlements_merchant_id_merchants_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (merchant_id) REFERENCES merchants(id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS stock_items (
  id serial PRIMARY KEY,
  merchant_id integer,
  name text NOT NULL,
  description text,
  cost numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL,
  emoji text,
  variations jsonb,
  is_active boolean DEFAULT true,
  created_at timestamp DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamp DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT stock_items_merchant_id_merchants_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (merchant_id) REFERENCES merchants(id)
);

-- api_keys must precede api_requests and webhook_deliveries, which reference it.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS api_keys (
  id serial PRIMARY KEY,
  merchant_id integer,
  key_name text NOT NULL,
  api_key text NOT NULL,
  key_prefix text NOT NULL,
  environment text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'sandbox',
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',
  permissions text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'create_transactions,read_transactions',
  webhook_url text,
  webhook_secret text,
  last_used_at timestamp,
  rate_limit_per_hour integer DEFAULT 1000,
  created_at timestamp DEFAULT now(),
  expires_at timestamp,
  CONSTRAINT api_keys_api_key_unique UNIQUE (api_key),
  CONSTRAINT api_keys_merchant_id_merchants_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (merchant_id) REFERENCES merchants(id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS api_requests (
  id serial PRIMARY KEY,
  api_key_id integer,
  merchant_id integer,
  endpoint text NOT NULL,
  method text NOT NULL,
  status_code integer NOT NULL,
  response_time integer,
  ip_address text,
  user_agent text,
  request_size integer,
  response_size integer,
  error_message text,
  created_at timestamp DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT api_requests_api_key_id_api_keys_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (api_key_id) REFERENCES api_keys(id),
  CONSTRAINT api_requests_merchant_id_merchants_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (merchant_id) REFERENCES merchants(id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS webhook_deliveries (
  id serial PRIMARY KEY,
  api_key_id integer,
  merchant_id integer,
  transaction_id integer,
  event_type text NOT NULL,
  webhook_url text NOT NULL,
  payload text NOT NULL,
  http_status integer,
  response_body text,
  attempt_count integer DEFAULT 1,
  max_attempts integer DEFAULT 3,
  next_retry_at timestamp,
  delivered_at timestamp,
  failed_at timestamp,
  created_at timestamp DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT webhook_deliveries_api_key_id_api_keys_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (api_key_id) REFERENCES api_keys(id),
  CONSTRAINT webhook_deliveries_merchant_id_merchants_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (merchant_id) REFERENCES merchants(id),
  CONSTRAINT webhook_deliveries_transaction_id_transactions_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (transaction_id) REFERENCES transactions(id)
);

COMMIT;

-- prod, which already have all of it. It records history, it does not change
-- either database. Nothing here backfills or infers data.
--
-- windcave_api_key / windcave_merchant_id are credential columns. They are
-- created empty and are never seeded.

BEGIN;

ALTER TABLE merchants
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS google_id text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS director text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS nzbn text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS custom_logo_url text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS windcave_api_key text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS windcave_merchant_id text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS theme_id text DEFAULT 'classic',
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS daily_goal numeric(10, 2) DEFAULT '500.00',
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS reset_token text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS reset_token_expiry timestamp;

-- One-off non-rent charges: `kind` distinguishes them from rent, `charge_type`
-- and `description` label them, and the two document_* columns carry the
-- optional attachment shown to the tenant at checkout.
ALTER TABLE invoices_rent_requests
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS kind text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'rent',
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS charge_type text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS description text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS document_url text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS document_name text;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS refunds (
  id serial PRIMARY KEY,
  transaction_id integer,
  merchant_id integer,
  refund_amount numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL,
  refund_reason text,
  refund_method text DEFAULT 'original_payment_method',
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
  windcave_refund_id text,
  windcave_fee_refunded numeric(10, 2) DEFAULT '0.00',
  platform_fee_refunded numeric(10, 2) DEFAULT '0.00',
  initiated_by text,
  customer_notified boolean DEFAULT false,
  completed_at timestamp,
  created_at timestamp DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT refunds_transaction_id_transactions_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (transaction_id) REFERENCES transactions(id),
  CONSTRAINT refunds_merchant_id_merchants_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (merchant_id) REFERENCES merchants(id)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS refunds_transaction_id_idx
  ON refunds (transaction_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS refunds_merchant_id_idx
  ON refunds (merchant_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS merchant_settlements (
  id serial PRIMARY KEY,
  merchant_id integer,
  settlement_period text NOT NULL,
  total_transaction_amount numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL,
  total_windcave_fees numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL,
  total_platform_fees numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL,
  net_settlement_amount numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
  settlement_date timestamp,
  created_at timestamp DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT merchant_settlements_merchant_id_merchants_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (merchant_id) REFERENCES merchants(id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS stock_items (
  id serial PRIMARY KEY,
  merchant_id integer,
  name text NOT NULL,
  description text,
  cost numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL,
  emoji text,
  variations jsonb,
  is_active boolean DEFAULT true,
  created_at timestamp DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamp DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT stock_items_merchant_id_merchants_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (merchant_id) REFERENCES merchants(id)
);

-- api_keys must precede api_requests and webhook_deliveries, which reference it.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS api_keys (
  id serial PRIMARY KEY,
  merchant_id integer,
  key_name text NOT NULL,
  api_key text NOT NULL,
  key_prefix text NOT NULL,
  environment text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'sandbox',
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',
  permissions text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'create_transactions,read_transactions',
  webhook_url text,
  webhook_secret text,
  last_used_at timestamp,
  rate_limit_per_hour integer DEFAULT 1000,
  created_at timestamp DEFAULT now(),
  expires_at timestamp,
  CONSTRAINT api_keys_api_key_unique UNIQUE (api_key),
  CONSTRAINT api_keys_merchant_id_merchants_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (merchant_id) REFERENCES merchants(id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS api_requests (
  id serial PRIMARY KEY,
  api_key_id integer,
  merchant_id integer,
  endpoint text NOT NULL,
  method text NOT NULL,
  status_code integer NOT NULL,
  response_time integer,
  ip_address text,
  user_agent text,
  request_size integer,
  response_size integer,
  error_message text,
  created_at timestamp DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT api_requests_api_key_id_api_keys_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (api_key_id) REFERENCES api_keys(id),
  CONSTRAINT api_requests_merchant_id_merchants_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (merchant_id) REFERENCES merchants(id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS webhook_deliveries (
  id serial PRIMARY KEY,
  api_key_id integer,
  merchant_id integer,
  transaction_id integer,
  event_type text NOT NULL,
  webhook_url text NOT NULL,
  payload text NOT NULL,
  http_status integer,
  response_body text,
  attempt_count integer DEFAULT 1,
  max_attempts integer DEFAULT 3,
  next_retry_at timestamp,
  delivered_at timestamp,
  failed_at timestamp,
  created_at timestamp DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT webhook_deliveries_api_key_id_api_keys_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (api_key_id) REFERENCES api_keys(id),
  CONSTRAINT webhook_deliveries_merchant_id_merchants_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (merchant_id) REFERENCES merchants(id),
  CONSTRAINT webhook_deliveries_transaction_id_transactions_id_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (transaction_id) REFERENCES transactions(id)
);

COMMIT;

Done. Step 5's catch-up migration is written and the rebuildability gate passes.

## Files left in the working tree (uncommitted, unstaged)

- **`/home/runner/workspace/migrations/0017_schema_history_catchup.sql`** (new) — the deliverable.
- **`/home/runner/workspace/server/migration-baseline-contract.ts`** (+15 lines) — **companion edit you did not ask for, flagged for your review.** `server/__tests__/migration-baseline-contract.test.ts:11` asserts that the set of migrations covered by `BASELINE_EFFECT_REQUIREMENTS` equals `listMigrationFiles()` exactly, so adding a migration file without a contract entry breaks that test and makes `--baseline` report `0017…: no baseline verification contract`. I added 14 requirement rows for `0017` (a representative column per altered table, all six tables, the `refunds_merchant_id_idx` index, and the `api_keys_api_key_unique` constraint). Both migration test suites pass (7 tests).

## Drift numbers

Measured empirically by building a scratch DB from `migrations/` alone and diffing against `shared/schema.ts` via `information_schema.columns` (table/column inventory sourced from Drizzle's own `getTableConfig`, so no regex parsing of `schema.ts`):

| | tables | columns |
|---|---|---|
| **Before** (`migrations/` minus `0017`) | **6** | **15** |
| **After** (full `migrations/`) | **0** | **0** |

The 6/15 reproduce the plan's list exactly. After: 29 tables declared, 29 built, 0 extra tables, 0 extra columns, 0 type mismatches. The static `drift.mjs` agrees (0/0).

Extra checks the gate ran beyond what you asked:
- **Idempotency:** re-executed `0017`'s statements against a database that already had all of it, snapshotting every column, constraint and index before and after — **0 changes**. It is genuinely inert.
- **No-op against the real databases:** read-only probe (`SET default_transaction_read_only = on`) of dev and prod confirms both already have all 6 tables and all 15 columns — missing tables `none`, missing columns `none` on both.
- Migrations were applied through the app's own `runPendingMigrations`, so the `BEGIN;`/`COMMIT;` trap is handled exactly as production handles it — each file on its own, transaction control stripped.

## Scratch databases

`taptpay_scratch_ac5541d23e` (before-run), `taptpay_scratch_5b39a041fe` and `taptpay_scratch_45c8e7c454` (intermediate), `taptpay_scratch_21713d44a1` (final gate run). All created on the `helium` server via the `postgres` maintenance database and **all dropped**; each run verifies its own drop by re-querying `pg_database`. Final audit: `scratch dbs remaining: NONE`; the server now holds `heliumdb, postgres, taptpay_verifier_tmp, template0, template1` — `taptpay_verifier_tmp` was already there before I started (it belongs to `verify-server-postgres.mjs`), it is not mine.

## Other gates

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — **silent**, exit 0.
- `npm run db:migrate:status` (read-only) — dev now reports **18 applied, 1 pending, 0 drifted, 0 orphaned**, the one pending being `0017`. Note this differs from the plan's §1 snapshot: Step 0 has evidently been done since the plan was written, so dev is at 18, not 15. Nothing was applied by me, to dev or prod.
- No `drizzle-kit push`, no `db:migrate`. I did run `drizzle-kit **generate**` — purely file-based, no DB connection — into a scratchpad output directory to get authoritative DDL for the column types, defaults and constraint names; `migrations/` and `migrations/meta/` were not touched by it.

## Things in `shared/schema.ts` I could not translate faithfully

1. **`merchant_subscriptions.tier` is nullable in `schema.ts` but `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free'` in the built database.** Pre-existing — `0010a` creates it that way, it reproduces identically without `0017`, and dev matches the migration (`is_nullable: NO`). Out of scope, so I left it; the gate reports it as a warning rather than failing on it. It is the only nullability disagreement in the whole schema.

2. **Rogue FK auto-increment defaults exist on dev but not in a fresh build.** Dev carries `DEFAULT nextval(...)` on `refunds.transaction_id`, `refunds.merchant_id` and `merchant_settlements.merchant_id` — the `db-schema-drift-fk-sequences` bug. `schema.ts` declares plain `integer`, so `0017` creates them plain, meaning **a database built from `migrations/` is correct and dev/prod are the drifted ones**. Because `0017` must be a pure no-op I deliberately did *not* add the `ALTER COLUMN … DROP DEFAULT` repair that `0010a:25-26` performs for `transactions.merchant_id`. That repair is a real, separate, non-no-op migration someone should decide on.

3. **Column order differs on dev for `stock_items`** (`emoji`/`variations` are last there, mid-table in `schema.ts`). Cosmetic only, not expressible without a rewrite, and not part of any gate.

Everything else — types, precision/scale, nullability, defaults, the `api_keys_api_key_unique` constraint, and both `refunds` indexes — translated exactly, and the FK constraint names match Drizzle's convention and what dev already has (e.g. `refunds_transaction_id_transactions_id_fk`).
